mechanism_narrative: The observed slight week-on-week recovery in RETAIL_REC mobility over the last two weeks, from its lowest point, indicates a slow but persistent underlying trend towards increased out-of-home activity, which will continue to lift retail and recreation visits over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: The mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than the mean of the last 28 days, despite the preceding two-week recovery.

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in RESIDENTIAL mobility, indicating people are spending less time at home, will directly free up time and opportunity for out-of-home activities, including retail and recreation, driving an increase over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls below 15.0 percent change from baseline in the next week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase over the next 14 days, even if RESIDENTIAL mobility drops below 15.0 percent change from baseline.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT mobility signals a stronger return to physical work and commuting patterns. This combined increase will generate more incidental foot traffic and demand for retail and recreation over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both increase by at least 1 percentage point week-on-week for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not increase, despite WORKPLACES and TRANSIT showing sustained increases for two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: The recent significant increase in PARKS mobility, despite winter conditions, suggests a growing public comfort with leaving home. If this comfort extends to other public spaces, it will drive an increase in retail and recreation visits over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days does not increase, even if PARKS mobility remains high or continues to rise.

mechanism_narrative: Given the extremely low current RETAIL_REC levels, any minor policy adjustment or public perception of easing restrictions will trigger a rapid, albeit small, rebound in retail and recreation mobility over the next week, as pent-up demand is released.
candidate_trigger: RETAIL_REC increases by more than 3 percentage points week-on-week in the next week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase in the subsequent week, despite an initial week-on-week increase of more than 3 percentage points.

mechanism_narrative: The approaching holiday season (mid-December) will drive a temporary, albeit constrained, increase in essential and discretionary shopping. This seasonal demand will lead to a modest uplift in both GROCERY_PHARM and RETAIL_REC mobility over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC and GROCERY_PHARM mobility do not show an increase over the next 14 days, indicating holiday demand is fully suppressed.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained high level of RESIDENTIAL mobility, indicating continued adherence to stay-at-home behaviors, will directly suppress any potential recovery in out-of-home activities, leading to lower RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL remains above 16.0 percent change from baseline for the next two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than the last 28 days, despite RESIDENTIAL mobility remaining above 16.0 percent for two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: Persistently low WORKPLACES and TRANSIT mobility reflects a depressed economic environment and reduced commuting. This lack of underlying economic activity and associated foot traffic will continue to suppress discretionary retail and recreation spending over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both remain below -45.0 percent change from baseline for the next two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than the last 28 days, despite WORKPLACES and TRANSIT remaining below -45.0 percent for two consecutive weeks.
